children: Asian currencies consolidate against the dollar, but may be supported by mild appetite for risk assets. Wall Street delivered a "broadly constructive performance" on Tuesday, UOB Global Economics & Markets Research says in a note. "Overall, markets appeared to take comfort from easing energy price pressures," UOB says. However, "investors remain focused on persistent inflation risks, central bank tightening expectations, and an increasingly busy earnings calendar," it adds. The U.S. dollar is 0.1% higher at 158.34 yen, but is little changed at 1,326.30 won, while the Australian dollar is up 0.1% at US$0.7011, LSEG data show. (ronnie.harui@wsj.com)
